messages:
aditya: FYI - ran into a weird onboarding snag today. The sample app README shows different env var names across language examples (REDWOOD_API_KEY in Node, REDWOOD_API_TOKEN in Go, and RW_API_KEY in Rust). New users are copying the wrong one and hitting 401s.
norma: Yikes. That's a classic snippet drift problem. Can you paste the Go and Rust snippets you're seeing?
aditya: Go example in README currently:
```go
package main
import (
  "net/http"
  "os"
)
func main() {
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", nil)
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_TOKEN"))
  // ...
}
```
Rust has:
```rust
use std::env;
let key = env::var("RW_API_KEY").unwrap();
// set header Authorization: Token <key>
```
ben: That's a mess. We should standardize everything to REDWOOD_API_KEY and use "Bearer" everywhere. Also update the Rust example to show reqwest usage with header and mention Windows vs POSIX env var syntax.
norma: Agree. Suggest replacement snippets that are copy/paste friendly and explicitly show where to set env vars. Also add a short "Common copy/paste mistakes" bullet in README and link to onboarding checklist.
aditya: Proposed unified snippets:
```bash
# POSIX
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<key>"
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'

# PowerShell
$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = "<key>"
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
```go
// Go (net/http)
import "os"
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
```
```rust
// Rust (reqwest)
let key = std::env::var("REDWOOD_API_KEY").expect("set REDWOOD_API_KEY");
let client = reqwest::blocking::Client::new();
let res = client.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate")
  .bearer_auth(key)
  .json(&serde_json::json!({"prompt":"hi"}))
  .send()?;
```
ben: Nice. Also add a tiny note: "If you see 401s, double-check you didn't copy legacy RW_* keys or use 'Token' instead of 'Bearer' in curl headers." That helped reduce two support tickets today.
norma: Can someone open a PR to update README and add a lint rule that flags RW_API_KEY, REDWOOD_API_TOKEN, and header prefixes 'Authorization: Token'? We should block merges that introduce those.
aditya: I'll open the PR and include a small test in docs-lint to grep for those bad patterns.
doc-robot: Current README: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/blob/main/samples/sample-app/README.md
snippets-lint: docs-lint run scheduled once PR is up. We can add the new regex checks to the snippet-check step.
onboard-bot: @onboarding FYI - will add checklist item: "use quick-copy button for snippets and verify env var names" to reduce manual copy/paste errors.
ben: Also consider adding language-specific quickstart pages instead of one combined README - that reduces cross-language drift. Might be bigger change but worth discussing.
norma: Good idea for follow-up. For now let's ship the README fix + lint rule. Thanks Aditya.
aditya: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1050  updates snippets + adds lint regex. CI queued.
snippets-lint: docs-lint: snippet-check FAILED on refs/pull/1050/head - found deprecated key "RW_API_KEY" at README.md:112. Please update.
aditya: Fixing now. Will update all occurrences and push.
ben: Once merged, let's notify Support & Onboarding so they can clear any open tickets referencing old keys.
aditya: Done. Merged and backported to v1-readme. Deployed to docs staging. Closing loop. :white_check_mark:
